| 2 | main talk | The Problem: Why Single-Pass LLMs Fail | Problem. One LLM pass gives a star with no second opinion, no evidence and no check on its explanation; sarcasm, mixed reviews and neighbouring stars trip it up. Keep it to 1 minute; the rest of the talk shows how Phase 2 fixes each point. |
| 3 | main talk | The Paper We Chose: What It Does | The paper we chose. Four cards, left to right: the task (one model rates a review 1-5 and justifies it), the data steps (TextBlob cleaning, equal per star, varied wording, extra neutral), the model (LLaMA-3-8B with a small LoRA add-on, exact Table 1 settings), and the prompt (rubric, one example, step-by-step). Then the reported 92.6%. Say: we rebuilt exactly this as Phase 1. |
| 4 | main talk | Why It Falls Short | Why it falls short. Four reasons in plain words: one pass with nothing to catch mistakes; the score depends heavily on the set-up (a leaked example, a skewed test, leak-free it is 54%); the data cleaning removes most negative reviews; and the justifications are a template. Be fair: the leak was in our first reproduction's example choice, not a claim about the authors. Next: two slides on how the method works, then three slides of evidence. |
| 5 | main talk | Phase 1 Data Preprocessing Pipeline | Original paper's pipeline (TextBlob DQC, stratified, VGST, neutral oversampling). Point forward: slide 9 shows TextBlob filtering hurts on Electronics. |
| 6 | main talk | Phase 1: LLaMA-3-8B + LoRA Fine-Tuning | LoRA explained. LoRA is still trained (Phase 1), but in the final stack it is an ablation row, not the main agent. |
| 7 | main talk | The One-Shot Label Leak Inflated Earlier Numbers | Leak audit. Picking a one-shot example whose star differs from the truth leaks about 8 points. All later numbers are zero-shot and leak-free. |
| 8 | main talk | Phase 1's Justifications Are a Template | Hallucination study. LoRA explanations are a canned template; digit probabilities are the usable signal. That is why Phase 2 combines probabilities, not explanations. |
| 9 | main talk | TextBlob Filtering Hurts; VGST Adds Nothing | Preprocessing ablation. TextBlob DQC deletes most 1 and 2 star reviews; VGST picks long reviews; both are dropped. |
| 10 | main talk | Where Phase 2 Started: the Original Four-Agent Design | Original Phase 2 design (Analyst, Visual, RAG, Critic). Say: this was the starting design; the Oct 9 audit (Run 2) and later experiments replaced it with the probe + Evidence + Reflector system (slide 14). Slide 12 maps each problem to its fix. |
| 11 | main talk | Phase 2 System: How a Review Is Rated and Explained | Phase 2 system. Walk the five boxes left to right. Decision core: Evidence model, LLaMA probe, Reflector (the main stack, built and frozen). Agentic layer: Router with escalation, the Hand-off agent, Explainer and Critic loop, all built in LangGraph and measured on the 3,000 test reviews (LLM re-rating was tested and dropped). Self-correction happens at three points: escalation, re-rating, and the explanation loop. |
| 12 | main talk | How Phase 2 Answers Each Shortcoming | How Phase 2 answers each shortcoming. Read the left column as the problems the audience just saw, then the fix, then the number that checks it. Spend time on three rows: two agents instead of one pass; LLMs explain and check instead of judging (because the judge failed twice); and template justifications replaced by evidence-based explanations checked by a Critic. All rows are now measured: escalation 92 vs 50 and 152 vs 78; explanations faithful 60-63% to 89% with 0 broken. |
| 13 | main talk | Phase 1 Results: The Baseline Paper's Method | Phase 1 results. First the data line in the subtitle: one dataset, splits drawn once and disjoint by review id and exact text, every choice made on dev, test sets read once (this answers any leakage question). Then: this is the baseline paper's method retrained on Electronics, leak-free. Exact star 54.0 / 53.4, but within one star about 94% and positive vs negative 91-93%: it gets the direction right. On the paper's own Kaggle data with its protocol and no leak it reaches 69.1% (always-5 gives 63.8%). The paper's 92.6% used a different protocol; our old 70.7 / 60.1 were leaky and withdrawn. |
| 14 | main talk | Main System: LLaMA Probe + Evidence Model Stack | MAIN RESULT. The main stack (= Probe + Evidence stack: LLaMA probe reads meaning, Evidence model reads key words, Reflector combines them) gets 67.5% on balanced eval and 75.7% on natural test, macro-F1 .675 / .612; 5 seeds 65.8 +/- 0.6 and 75.4 +/- 0.8. If asked whether that is good: exact five-star rating is hard because neighbouring stars are ambiguous; random is 20%, base LLaMA 34%, SVM ~48%, DistilBERT 53%, Phase 1 54%; we are within one star 97% of the time. Read the honest-read band aloud. |
| 15 | main talk | How Far Phase 2 Moves the Baseline | Phase 1 to Phase 2. Lead with the gain: +13.5 points on balanced eval and +22.3 on natural test, 29% and 48% fewer errors, significant after Holm. Then why: the agents complement (Evidence model on short reviews, probe on long ones). Say the caveat yourself: the earlier stack refit on the same dev reviews is only 2.0 / 1.5 behind. Never quote 70.7 / 60.1 (leaky), 74.8 (one seed) or 79.9 (class-mix correction). |
| 16 | main talk | Hand-Off Agent: Answer When Sure, Ask a Person When Not | Hand-off agent. Say: accuracy has plateaued at about 67 / 76, so the agentic answer is to know when you are unsure. The Hand-off agent answers automatically only when the stack is confident; the threshold was fixed on dev2 before the test sets were read. On natural test it answers 56% of reviews and is right 93% of the time; on balanced eval 85% on 42%. What it hands to a person is only 54-55% right, so those are the hard ones. Phase 1 with the same rule reaches only 67-68%. |
| 17 | main talk | Where the Main Stack Is Right, and Where It Errs | Results in detail. Left: confusion matrix, mistakes hug the diagonal, 90% of errors are one star off. Right: per-star recall, Phase 1 vs Phase 2. Be honest about the one exception: on natural test Phase 1 finds more 4-star reviews, because it over-predicts 4-star; Phase 2 is far better on 5-star, the most common class. |
| 18 | main talk | Why Two Agents Beat One | Why it works. Left: the Evidence model wins on short reviews, the LLaMA probe on long reviews, the stack is best or near-best in every length band. Right: when the two agents disagree, the stack still gets 56% right, versus 36-50% for either alone. That is the case for stacking two different kinds of signal. Hard cases (band): reviews that sound negative but are rated 4-5 stars, +28 points over Phase 1 on both test sets; positive-sounding 1-2 star reviews +15 on natural test; mixed reviews: small or no gain; explicit sarcasm is too rare to measure (6 and 1 reviews). |
| 19 | main talk | Everything We Tried and Dropped | Full ledger (one slide; the last two rows are the 120K probe, which added only +0.3 on dev2 so the 40K probe stays, and the Instruct-LLM re-rating, 76 fixed vs 89 broken, the third LLM-judge failure). Do not read every row. Pick three: the LLM judge (failed twice, which is why the LLM does not decide the star), the Visual Verifier (constant output), and the recalibration (the gain was the leak). Say: every rule was written before the run, on dev data only. |
| 20 | main talk | What We Kept, and the Evidence for It | What we kept. Walk the ten rows quickly: each change has its evidence on the right. Together they give the main stack, 67.5% balanced eval and 75.7% natural test. |
| 21 | main talk | Does the Result Hold Up? Corrections, Errors, Calibration, Cost | Robustness. After Holm correction 5 of 8 comparisons stay significant, including the main stack vs the earlier LoRA + Evidence stack on both splits. Most errors are one star off. Calibration is good (ECE .05-.06). The probe costs 0.67 s per review, the rest is under 0.1 ms: that is why the next step adds a Router. |
| 22 | main talk | Self-Correction 1: Two Stars Fixed for Each One Broken | Self-correction 1, measured. Say: the Evidence model gives a quick draft; when it is unsure, the LLaMA probe is called and the Reflector revises the star. On the test sets the revision fixed 92 stars and broke 50 on balanced eval, 152 vs 78 on natural test, both highly significant. And LLaMA was skipped on 39-48% of reviews with no accuracy change. Be open that this was the second attempt: the first threshold failed its natural-dev check by 0.3 points and was never tested. |
| 23 | main talk | Self-Correction 3: The Critic Makes Explanations Faithful | Self-correction 3, measured. Say: the Explainer writes a short explanation from the evidence only; the Critic checks five things (star, quotes really in the review, key phrases, disagreement, no invented claims) and sends it back with specific feedback. First drafts are faithful 60-63% of the time; after the loop 89%, and it never broke a good one (793 fixed, 0 broken). The deletion test shows the cited phrases are what the decision depends on. Compare with Phase 1: its justification never quotes the review and is one of 5 stock sentences. Be open: about 11% still fail a check. |
| 24 | main talk | Phase 2 v3 Build Schedule | Build schedule, Oct 25 to Nov 5. Say: every row has its rule written first and is logged. The bigger probe failed its check (+0.3 on dev2), so the 40K probe stays. The explanations and Critic loop ran on all 3,000 test reviews (faithful 60-63% to 89%, 0 broken), then the deletion test; report, paper tables, hard cases and the demo notebook are done. Freeze stage 1 on Nov 1, stage 2 on Nov 5. |
| 25 | main talk | Conclusions | Conclusions. Four cards: Phase 1 reproduced honestly (and two problems found in the original protocol); Phase 2's two-agent stack beats the single fine-tuned model, significantly; the agentic layer is measured (escalation fixes about two stars per one broken, the Critic loop makes 89% of explanations faithful with none broken, the Hand-off agent is 93% right on the 56% it answers); and the limits, said plainly (one dataset, part of the gain from the bigger fit set, sarcasm too rare to measure). End with the dates: freeze Nov 1 / 5, draft Nov 8, submit Nov 20, final presentation in December. |
